doc_friction.issue: Lists audits already done but not the checks a new venture must pass (sibling link, thousands split, front-matter lengths); I found them only from a failing local CI run. A one-line pointer to run_workflow_locally.py --for-changes before the first push would save a cycle.
Says to search open PRs with search_pull_requests MCP; that tool is not exposed in cloud sessions, gh api search/issues works (as other runs reported).

Its unwired tree checks (thousands split, CSV comma split, date digit boundary) only surface one at a time across local runs; each needed a full ~3 min rerun. A '--new-venture' mode that runs just the tree checks on one directory would be faster.

notes: Explore idea: extreme value analysis as a research-algorithm tool (ventures/extreme-value-analysis), since the repository had nothing for tail events. GEV/Gumbel MLE on annual maxima, GPD on runs-declustered POT, profile-likelihood and delta intervals, threshold stability, mean residual life, linear-trend GEV with LR test, design-life risk. Matches scipy 1.18.1 to <=1e-5 (2e-9..4e-8 on USGS Potomac). Seeded coverage (400 reps x 4): delta 84-86% at n=30-60, profile 93-94% (96.5% at n=100). Finding: 20 water years of Potomac data give a 100-year flow ~200k cfs vs 411,617 from 96 years of peaks; instantaneous peaks of the same 20 years give 203,047, so the record length, not daily-mean vs peak, causes it. Local CI after fixes: see PR body. No separate docs/reports agent doc: the README's Verification and research-tools README candidates carry what the next run needs.
